title: Godot 4.6 fails to render with XR stereoscopic shaders using Direct3D 12
body:
### Tested versions

* Reproducible in: Godot version 4.6 beta 1 (mono build)
* Reproducible in: Godot version 4.6 dev 6 (standard build)
* ***Not*** reproducible in: Godot version 4.6 dev 5 (standard build)

### System information

Godot v4.6.beta1.mono - Windows 11 (build 22631) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9144) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-14900KF (32 threads) - 63.83 GiB memory

### Issue description

Launching a barebones XR project while Direct3D is the active driver results in a black screen, and many errors per second.

The following errors repeat every frame:
```
ERROR: Create(Graphics)PipelineState failed with error 0x80070057.
ERROR: servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp:4224 - Condition "!pipeline.driver_id" is true. Returning: RID()
ERROR: servers/rendering/renderer_rd/pipeline_cache_rd.cpp:59 - Condition "pipeline.is_null()" is true. Returning: RID()
ERROR: servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp:4665 - Parameter "pipeline" is null.
ERROR: This render pipeline requires (0) bytes of push constant data, supplied: (64)
ERROR: No render pipeline was set before attempting to draw.
```

Changing "Rendering > Rendering Device > Driver.windows" to "vulkan" and restarting the editor fixes the issue.

As for the VR headset I'm using when testing, I'm using a Quest 3S and Virtual Desktop configured to VXDR as the OpenXR Runtime. (Interestingly, Virtual Desktop becomes completely unresponsive too, making me unable to open the steam overlay nor the virtual desktop mode, once the program is running.)

### Steps to reproduce

Project is just a brand new project using the "Mobile" renderer, with the following steps taken:
* "Project Settings > XR > Shaders > Enabled" set to true
* A basic Node3D as the main scene, with a XROrigin3D child (which itself has a XRCamera3D child)

Changing "Rendering > Rendering Device > Driver.windows" to "vulkan" and restarting the editor fixes the issue.

As for the VR headset I'm using when testing, I'm using a Quest 3S and Virtual Desktop configured to VXDR as the OpenXR Runtime. (Interestingly, Virtual Desktop becomes completely unresponsive too, making me unable to open the steam overlay nor the virtual desktop mode, once the program is running.)

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[godotcrashtest-2.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24225698/godotcrashtest-2.zip)
